description:
FILED s515a (Opus, 2026-10-11) from the #3184 detector recount (gate: 4 sites in file-glob-shim-01.t's program).
`use File::Glob qw(:bsd_glob); glob("dir/a b.txt")` -- the VALUE is perl's (1 result, the space kept: the runtime reaches the caller's glob override), but under PCL_DETECT=announce the call site is announced: "'main::glob' was parsed as the built-in but code that ran at line 1 installed a sub with no prototype".  The File::Glob facts overlay lists `glob` in the :bsd_glob tag, and builtin_is_overridable('glob') is true, so the builtin-override recorder should have recorded it -- either the `glob(...)` call parse does not consult the override registry (glob has its own parse path for `<*.c>`), or the overlay's tag does not reach _use_imported_names.  Effect today: noise only (one stderr line per site under announce; nothing under the default `off`).  Probe: scratch/s515a/pr/bsdg.pl in the s515a worktree.


LOCATED s516 (Fable, 2026-10-12, review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p516c/ovr.pl): under `use File::Glob qw(:bsd_glob)` the parse DOES consult the override -- every glob(...) call site is emitted as (pl-glob ...), the override-aware call, and the value is perl in list, scalar, <> and iterator shapes -- yet the detector table at the top of the unit registers each site as ("main" "glob" N "builtin").  So the TABLE is wrong, not the parse: the recorder lists a site as "builtin" although the emission took the override; fix the table entry (or its kind) where the override-aware emission is chosen, and the 4 gate lines go away.  Sibling finding #2879: the quoted-string spelling use File::Glob ':bsd_glob' takes the OTHER branch (p-glob, the builtin -- a real silent wrong), so the two tasks share one brief.
subject: use File::Glob qw(:bsd_glob): the detector announces every glob() call as a displaced built-in (value is perl's; the parse ignores the recorded override) -- the gate's last 4 detector sites
